trial_court: Civil Judge (Senior Division), Chhatrapur, Ganjam (MAT Case No.20 of 2019)
case_name: Laxmi Narayan Samantaray vs Snigdharani Mangaraj Opposite Party
facts_of_case: The wife filed a petition under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, while the husband initiated a proceeding under Section 9 of the same act. The wife was staying at Chhatrapur as she had been transferred to U.Co Bank, Chhatrapur Branch.

legal_principles.principle: A proceeding under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act cannot be transferred merely because an application under Section 9 is filed at a different location.
legal_principles.held: It is in this view of the matter, this Court finds no difficulty in undertaking of the proceeding under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act by the wife at Chhatrapur and merely because an application under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act is filed at the instance of the husband at Bhubaneswar cannot be a ground for transfer of the MAT proceeding filed by the wife.

legal_principles.principle: A wife's residence does not affect her ability to file a petition under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: This Court finds there is no difficulty in undertaking of the proceeding under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act by the wife at Chhatrapur

outcome.final_order: The transfer application stands rejected with vacation of interim order dated 25.11.2019 passed by this Court in I.A.No,.422 of 2019.

use_for_drafting: drafting a divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
advising on transfer application in matrimonial case
